correctness.rationale: PASS: Reconstructed base-b carry identity t(bq+j)=t(q)+j and exact adjacent-pair relation c−a≡1 mod gcd(b−1,m), including a constructive realization using trailing (b−1) digits. Every four-window at b≥3 crosses at most one substitution-block boundary, hence two of its three adjacent increments equal +1; its reversal would require two −1 increments, impossible in one four-window for m≥3. Length-three reverse companions must be palindromes. Explicit three- and four-factor families have sizes 2m²/d−m and 3m²/d−2m by inclusion-exclusion; reversal of length-two pairs occurs exactly for d|2, giving displayed gcd trichotomy. Independent direct-prefix tests across 20 base/modulus combinations and three lengths were honest subset checks; 48/60 prefix counts were complete, 12 were not because prefixes do not necessarily realize the full infinite language. All 60 avoided contradictory reversals. Infinite result rests on constructive adjacency and substitution boundary proof.
